name: Lion
alt: A close-up photo of a large, golden-furred big cat with a thick mane, resting in tall grass.
facts: Adult males in this species grow a thick mane of fur around their head and neck.
It is one of the only big cats that lives and hunts in family groups.
The females in its family group do most of the hunting.

name: Tiger
alt: A close-up photo of a large orange-and-black striped big cat walking through jungle grass.
facts: This is the largest of all big cats, with bold stripes on its fur.
No two of these animals have the exact same stripe pattern — they're like fingerprints.
It is an excellent swimmer and often cools off in rivers and ponds.

name: Elephant
alt: A close-up photo of a huge gray animal with large ears, tusks, and a long trunk reaching toward the ground.
facts: This is the largest land animal on Earth, with big floppy ears and a long trunk.
It uses its trunk like a hand, to grab food, drink water, and even give itself a shower.
It lives in close family herds usually led by an older female.

name: Giraffe
alt: A close-up photo of a tall, patterned animal with a very long neck, reaching up to eat leaves from a tree.
facts: This is the tallest land animal in the world, thanks to its very long neck and legs.
Its tongue can be over a foot long and helps it reach leaves high in trees.
Each one has a unique pattern of patches, just like a person's fingerprint.

name: Zebra
alt: A close-up photo of a horse-like animal covered head to tail in bold black and white stripes.
facts: This animal is covered in stripes, and no two patterns are exactly alike.
It lives in herds on the open grasslands of Africa.
Scientists think its stripe pattern may help confuse biting flies and predators.

name: Panda
alt: A close-up photo of a round, black-and-white bear sitting and chewing on a bamboo stalk.
facts: This black-and-white animal spends most of its day eating bamboo.
A newborn of this species is pink, hairless, and smaller than a stick of butter.
It's become a symbol of wildlife conservation around the world.

name: Koala
alt: A close-up photo of a gray, round-eared animal clinging to a tree branch.
facts: This animal sleeps up to 20 hours a day, mostly in the branches of trees.
It eats almost nothing but eucalyptus leaves.
Despite its appearance, it isn't actually a bear — it's a marsupial that carries its baby in a pouch.

name: Kangaroo
alt: A close-up photo of a tan, long-legged animal balancing upright on its strong back legs and tail.
facts: This animal can leap more than three times its own body length in a single hop.
It carries its baby, called a joey, in a pouch on its belly.
It uses its strong tail for balance while hopping and even as a prop while standing still.

name: Gorilla
alt: A close-up photo of a large, dark-furred primate sitting calmly in green forest.
facts: This is one of the largest primates and is closely related to humans.
Adult males develop a patch of silver-gray fur on their backs as they age.
It mostly eats leaves, stems, and fruit, and lives in close family groups.

name: Chimpanzee
alt: A close-up photo of a small, dark-furred primate with an expressive face, sitting among green leaves.
facts: This is one of the closest living relatives to humans, sharing most of our DNA.
It is known for using simple tools, like sticks, to get food.
It lives in social groups and communicates with calls, gestures, and facial expressions.

name: Polar Bear
alt: A close-up photo of a huge white-furred bear standing on snow and ice.
facts: This is the largest land predator, living on Arctic ice and snow.
Its fur looks white but is actually clear, and the skin underneath is black.
It is an excellent swimmer and can paddle for many miles searching for food.

name: Brown Bear
alt: A close-up photo of a large, shaggy brown-furred animal standing near a forest stream.
facts: This large, shaggy animal can stand on its back legs to look around or reach food.
It eats almost anything, including berries, fish, and small animals.
It sleeps through the coldest months of winter in a long rest called hibernation.

name: Wolf
alt: A close-up photo of a gray, pointy-eared animal standing alert in a snowy forest.
facts: This animal lives and hunts in family groups called packs.
It can howl loudly to communicate with other members of its group from far away.
It is the wild ancestor of every breed of pet dog.

name: Fox
alt: A close-up photo of a small orange-furred animal with a pointed face and bushy tail.
facts: This small, clever animal has big pointed ears and a long bushy tail.
It uses its excellent hearing to find small animals hiding under snow.
It can be found living in forests, deserts, and even cities.

name: Cheetah
alt: A close-up photo of a slender, spotted cat crouched low and ready to sprint across grassland.
facts: This animal is the fastest land animal on Earth, able to reach incredible bursts of speed.
It has dark, tear-shaped marks running from its eyes down its face.
Unlike most big cats, it hunts mostly during the day.

name: Leopard
alt: A close-up photo of a spotted golden cat resting on a tree branch.
facts: This big cat has dark, rosette-shaped spots covering its golden fur.
It is incredibly strong and often drags its prey up into trees to keep it safe from other predators.
It is mostly active at night and is an excellent, silent climber.

name: Hippopotamus
alt: A close-up photo of a huge, round gray animal mostly submerged in muddy river water.
facts: This huge animal spends most of the day resting in rivers and lakes to stay cool.
Despite its size, it can run surprisingly fast on land.
Its skin produces a natural reddish oil that protects it like sunscreen.

name: Rhinoceros
alt: A close-up photo of a massive gray animal with thick skin and a large horn on its snout.
facts: This animal has one or two large horns made of the same material as human fingernails.
Its skin is extremely thick and tough, like natural armor.
Despite weighing as much as a small car, it can charge at surprising speed.

name: Crocodile
alt: A close-up photo of a long, scaly reptile floating at the surface of murky water with just its eyes and snout showing.
facts: This reptile can hold its breath underwater for over an hour.
It has one of the strongest bites of any animal alive.
It often floats almost completely still in the water, waiting to ambush prey.

name: Flamingo
alt: A close-up photo of a tall pink bird standing on one thin leg in shallow water.
facts: This bird's pink color comes from the shrimp and algae it eats.
It often stands and even sleeps balanced on just one leg.
Large groups of this bird gather together by the thousands in shallow lakes.

name: Peacock
alt: A close-up photo of a bird with a spectacular fan of blue and green eye-spotted tail feathers.
facts: The male of this bird species has a giant, colorful tail of feathers he fans out to attract mates.
His tail feathers are covered in shimmering blue and green eye-shaped spots.
Despite the huge tail, this bird can still fly short distances.

name: Owl
alt: A close-up photo of a round-faced bird with big forward-facing eyes, perched on a branch at night.
facts: This bird can turn its head almost all the way around to look behind itself.
It can fly almost silently, which helps it sneak up on prey at night.
Its eyes are so large that it can't move them — it has to turn its whole head to look around.

name: Eagle
alt: A close-up photo of a large bird of prey with a sharp curved beak, soaring with wings spread wide.
facts: This bird has incredibly sharp eyesight, letting it spot prey from high in the sky.
It builds huge nests, sometimes used and added to for many years.
Its strong, curved talons help it snatch fish right out of the water.

name: Penguin
alt: A close-up photo of a black-and-white bird standing upright on ice.
facts: This bird cannot fly, but it is an excellent swimmer, using its wings like flippers.
It huddles together in large groups to stay warm in freezing weather.
It waddles on land but glides gracefully underwater.

name: Dolphin
alt: A close-up photo of a sleek gray sea animal leaping out of blue ocean water.
facts: This intelligent ocean animal uses clicks and whistles to communicate with others.
It can leap high out of the water and is known for playful behavior.
It uses echolocation, bouncing sound off objects, to find food in murky water.

name: Octopus
alt: A close-up photo of a soft-bodied sea creature with eight long arms spread across a rocky reef.
facts: This sea animal has eight arms and can squeeze through incredibly tiny gaps.
It can change the color and texture of its skin to hide from danger.
It is considered one of the smartest invertebrates, able to solve puzzles and open jars.

name: Sea Turtle
alt: A close-up photo of a large turtle with a patterned shell swimming through clear blue ocean water.
facts: This animal can hold its breath for hours while resting underwater.
Females return to the very same beach where they were born to lay their own eggs.
It has a hard shell that protects it, but it cannot pull its flippers all the way inside like land turtles.

name: Shark
alt: A close-up photo of a large, gray fish with a pointed fin gliding through open ocean water.
facts: This ocean predator can sense a tiny amount of blood in the water from far away.
It has rows of sharp teeth that are constantly replaced throughout its life.
Some kinds of this fish must keep swimming constantly or they will sink.

name: Ostrich
alt: A close-up photo of a tall, long-necked bird with fluffy feathers standing on the open plains.
facts: This is the largest bird in the world, but it cannot fly at all.
It can run faster than any other bird, reaching very high speeds.
Its eyes are bigger than its brain.

name: Camel
alt: A close-up photo of a tan animal with one or two humps on its back, standing in a sandy desert.
facts: This animal can go for many days without drinking any water.
It stores fat, not water, in the hump on its back.
Its wide, padded feet keep it from sinking into soft desert sand.
